title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K_0 = R, K an algebraic closure (K = C), M a motive over R, e.g. M = Mot*(X) for X/R. On the previous page Grothendieck has two antilinear involutions on DR(M)_K = DR(M_K) ≅ H*(X(K),K). σ is complex conjugation of coefficients with respect to the Betti real structure H*(X(K),R); it does not respect the Hodge filtration. τ comes from the R-structure DR(M) ⊗_R K; it does respect the filtration. They commute, and στ = τσ = f_R is the C-linear automorphism induced by the antiholomorphic involution τ_X of X(K).

This page draws the conclusion. A motive over R defines:
(a) a Q-Hodge structure V = H*(X(C),Q);
(b) a Q-rational involution f_R = F_∞ of V. It is rational on V and real on V_R.
The compatibility condition is that f_R σ (= τ) preserves the Hodge filtration. Equivalently, f_R carries the Hodge filtration F to its conjugate F̄, i.e. F_∞ H^{p,q} = H^{q,p}. Reformulated: (b) is an isomorphism of V with the 'conjugate' Hodge structure. Grothendieck names this the 'Frobenius réel'.

Tannakian translation. Let G be the motivic Galois group of M over R (a Q-group). Then:
- f_R ∈ G(Q) has order ≤ 2.
- Its image generates G/G^0. Using Hodge-conjecture connectedness of the group of M_C, G/G^0 is Z/2 or trivial.
- f_R normalizes the Hodge cocharacter i = h: S_R → G_R (S = Res_{C/R} G_m) via f h(λ) f^{-1} = h(λ'), where λ ↦ λ' is the canonical conjugation of S.
- Restricted to the circle U_R this reads f h(λ) f^{-1} = h(λ^{-1}).
The left margin records the resulting datum (G/Q, h: S_R → G_R, weight/character ε: G → G_m, f_R ∈ G(Q)) subject to these conditions.

Final claim: the functor M ↦ (Hodge structure, F_∞) is fully faithful, assuming the Hodge conjecture. Indeed Hom_R(M,N) = Hom_C(M_C,N_C)^{Gal(C/R)}, the Hodge conjecture identifies Hom_C with Hodge classes, and Galois invariance is F_∞-invariance.

The next page then builds the 'twisted Betti' Q-structure W = V^+ ⊕ iV^- inside V_C, which is a Q-form of H_dR ⊗ R. W gives a second ⊗-fibre functor, not ⊗-isomorphic to Betti, differing by the cocycle defined by F_∞.
errors: 'Order 2' should be 'order ≤ 2' (e.g. F_∞ = 1 on Q(0)). Similarly G/G^0 may be trivial, e.g. for Q(1), where G = G_m and F_∞ = -1 ∈ G^0. The claim that the image generates G/G^0 is still correct.

Generation of G/G^0 by F_∞ tacitly uses connectedness of the motivic group of M_C (Mumford–Tate connectedness, which identifies with the motivic group via the Hodge conjecture). This is consistent with the page's reliance on the Hodge conjecture but is not stated.
Minor: V is a Q-Hodge structure; 'structure de Hodge sur K' just means its Hodge decomposition lives over K = C.

ideas.what: A motive over R gives a Q-Hodge structure plus an involution F_∞ (from complex conjugation on X(C)) exchanging H^{p,q} and H^{q,p}. Equivalently F_∞σ preserves the Hodge filtration, and this composite is the de Rham real structure.
ideas.modern_name: Real Hodge structure / Hodge realization of motives over R with real Frobenius F_∞
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979), §1; also standard in Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih (LNM 900, 1982)

ideas.what: Real Frobenius as an element f_R ∈ G(Q) of the motivic Galois group of M/R, of order ≤ 2, generating G/G^0, normalizing h: S → G_R via h(λ) ↦ h(λ̄), hence inverting h on U.
ideas.modern_name: F_∞ in the motivic/Mumford–Tate group; Shimura-datum-type compatibility of complex conjugation with h
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge cycles, Valeurs de fonctions L); Langlands (Taniyama group, 1979); Milne–Shih

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of motives over R into (Hodge structures with F_∞), conditional on the Hodge conjecture.
ideas.modern_name: Conditional full faithfulness of the Hodge realization over R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Deligne 1979 / Jannsen's 'Mixed motives and algebraic K-theory' discussions

ideas.what: Group-theoretic datum (G/Q, h: S_R → G_R, ε: G → G_m, f_R ∈ G(Q)) encoding the realization of motives over R.
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of real Hodge structures / motivic Galois group of R with complex conjugation

missed.claim: This is an early (c. 1969–72) private formulation of the real-Frobenius formalism for motives over R. It covers F_∞ in the motivic Galois group normalizing the Hodge cocharacter, and conditional full faithfulness. The formalism appears publicly only in Deligne 1979 and Deligne–Milne 1982. This documents priority and transmission rather than giving a new result.
missed.quote: f_R ∈ G(Q) dit frobenius réel. C'est un élément d'ordre 2 dont l'image dans G/G^0 engendre ce groupe. Cet élément normalise i : S_R → G_R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck had the F_∞/Hodge-cocharacter compatibility (the core of the Deligne-period and Shimura-datum formalism) in his motivic-Galois-group notes years before publication.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically standard today and essentially correct. It is a clean, early unpublished anticipation of Deligne's 1979 real Frobenius / real Hodge structure formalism inside a Tannakian motivic-Galois framework. The more interesting twisted-Betti fibre-functor observation is on the next page.
transcription_corrections: 'défini par l'aut σ_x de X(K)' should read 'défini par l'aut τ_X de X(K)' (τ with subscript X, consistent with the previous page).
'{(f_R)σ invariant[?] la filtration naturelle' is better read '(f_R)σ respecte la filtration naturelle', i.e. f_R exchanges the given filtration and its opposite.
'En termes de "domaine des données[?]"' is probably 'En termes de "structure de données"' or similar; uncertain.

Left margin: 'La structure en vue donne G sur Q, i: S_R → G_R (avec i|... défini sur Q etc.), ε: G → G_m, + f_R ∈ G(Q) satisfaisant à conditions' is plausible; 'i(...)' is likely i restricted to G_m (the weight), defined over Q.
